{{Quote|Two there should be; no more, no less. One to embody power, the other to crave it.|Darth Bane|<ref name="DB: PoD" />}}
The '''Rule of Two''' doctrine, also called the '''Banite system''' and known as '''Chwayatyun''' in [[Sith (language)|Sith]], was the guiding principle of the [[Order of the Sith Lords]] after the internecine [[New Sith Wars]]. It replaced the practices of [[Sith Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Skere Kaan|Kaan's]] [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]], which claimed equality among Sith Lords and forbade the use of the title "[[Darth/Legends|Darth]]."

The Rule of Two was instituted by [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]], once a student at Kaan's [[Sith academy]], in response to what he viewed as inevitable, self-destructive infighting within the [[Sith/Legends|Sith Order]]. The Rule of Two states that there would be only two Sith at one time, a [[Sith Master/Legends|master]] and an [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], guaranteeing that when the apprentice becomes powerful enough in the ways of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] to take the title of master, only then would they be worthy of the title. This transfer of power would only take place when the apprentice takes their master's life and finds a worthy student to repeat the cycle, this way the Sith will grow more powerful and still exist through the new master. Both master and apprentice were considered to be Sith Lords.

The practice survived with varying levels of enforcement for a thousand years until the murder of [[Darth Tenebrous/Legends|Darth Tenebrous]] at the hands of his apprentice in [[67 BBY/Legends|67 BBY]]&mdash; [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]] held the doctrine in contempt, and intended to live forever together with his own apprentice, [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]]. Although the latter betrayed and murdered his master in accordance with the Rule of Two and trained apprentices of his own, never more than one at the same time, he did not fully accept it, following instead his own [[Rule of One (Palpatine's Doctrine)|Rule of One]], in order for him to continue as the ruler of the Sith.

==History==
===Creation===
{{Quote|When your power eclipses mine I will become expendable. This is the Rule of Two: one Master and one apprentice. When you are ready to claim the mantle of Dark Lord as your own, you must do so by eliminating me.|Darth Bane, to Darth Zannah|<ref name="Darth Bane: Rule of Two">''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Essential_Legends_Rule_of_Two.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Darth Bane, Sith Master, and Darth Zannah, Sith apprentice; first in the order of the Rule of Two]]
In an attempt to avoid the seemingly inevitable clash between power hungry [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]] sought to reinvent the Sith Order with only two members&mdash;a [[Sith Master/Legends|Sith Master]], and an [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]]. Bane created the Rule of Two in a way which would prevent the Sith becoming like Kaan's [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]]; Darth Bane thought the Brotherhood was weak and decided he must destroy it, then rebuild the Sith order as otherwise they were doomed to fail like all Sith before them. He decided there should only be one apprentice because if there were multiple the strongest would be held back by the weaker apprentices, this also prevented the weaker apprentices joining together to defeat the more powerful master leaving the master to be replaced by someone weaker. Bane decided "One Sith must contain all the power of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]]. One Master must decide how that power should be used."<ref name="DB: PoD" />

His course of action decided, Bane destroyed the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]] in true Sith fashion by duping [[Sith Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Skere Kaan]] into using a [[The Force/Legends|Force]] technique he learned from his studies of the dark arts known as the [[Thought bomb]]. Lord Kaan gathered together every [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] in the Brotherhood as the Jedi were closing in to destroy them when he detonated the Thought bomb. Bane, knowing what would happen to Force-sensitive users within the bomb's range, escaped the Brotherhood's fate and hid from the surviving [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]. Bane was then free to start his new Sith Order implementing the Rule of Two with his newfound apprentice, [[Darth Zannah/Legends|Zannah]]. Through his actions, Bane fulfilled the prophecy of the [[Sith'ari/Legends|Sith'ari]] and ended the [[New Sith Wars]].<ref name="DB: PoD" />

For nearly 1,000 years, the [[Order of the Sith Lords|Sith]] watched and waited, destabilizing the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] whenever opportunity arose without revealing themselves. Around [[188 BBY]], during the [[Dark Jedi Conflict]], [[Kibh Jeen]] warned the Jedi that the Sith had survived and were operating utilizing the Rule of Two,<ref name="JvsS: TEGttF">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> though his warnings were mostly ignored or passed off as the rantings of a madman.<ref name="Evil Never Dies">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}}</ref>

===Prelude to the Empire===
{{Quote|Remember, the first and only reality of the Sith&hellip; there can only be two. And you are no longer my apprentice. You have been replaced.|Darth Sidious, to Darth Maul|<ref name="TCW|The Lawless">{{TCW|The Lawless}}</ref>}}
[[File:Legends-PlagueisCover.png|thumb|left|250px|Darth Plagueis and his apprentice, Darth Sidious]]
By the time of [[Darth Tenebrous/Legends|Rugess Nome/Darth Tenebrous]], the Sith had come to the conclusion that the Rule of Two had essentially expired, as the time was coming when they would finally gain their revenge over the hated [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. However, this was always the opinion of the Master only, as the apprentice was invariably in the same subservient position as when the Rule was first envisioned.<ref name="DP">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>

During this 1,000 year period, the [[Bith/Legends|Bith]] [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] Darth Tenebrous emerged, taking a [[Muun/Legends|Muun]], [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]] as his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]]. Regarding the Sith of the Rule of Two, Plagueis said there were "30 in a millennium rather than the tens of thousands fit to be Jedi." Plagueis eventually came to realize the Rule of Two was old and outdated. In [[67 BBY/Legends|67 BBY]], Plagueis [[Incident on Bal'demnic|betrayed and killed]] his master on [[Bal'demnic/Legends|Bal'demnic]], becoming the new Dark Lord of the Sith, but not before declaring that the Rule of Two ended with them. Shortly after arriving at [[Sojourn (moon)|Sojourn]], Plagueis discovered that Tenebrous broke the Rule of Two whilst training him, as he had taken a fellow Bith as an apprentice, dubbing him [[Darth Venamis]]. The mantle of [[Sith Master/Legends|Sith Master]] ultimately went to Plagueis, not Venamis, after Plagueis [[Contest on Sojourn|bested]] him in a duel. After defeating Venamis, Plagueis discovered that Venamis had kept a list of potential apprentices in case he would have succeeded in killing him: a [[Shi'ido]] [[Changeling/Legends|changeling]], an [[Iktotchi/Legends|Iktotchi]] [[Unidentified Iktotchi prophet|prophet]] and the demented [[Nautolan/Legends|Nautolan]] [[Naat Lare]], but Plagueis eliminated the former two and Lare [[Duel on Abraxin|failed]] to fulfill Plagueis' expectations. [[65 BBY/Legends|Two years later]], Plagueis took the human [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] as his apprentice, inducting him into the Order as Darth Sidious, and had intended to rule alongside him forever. However, wanting all the power for himself, Sidious became the Dark Lord of the Sith by betraying and murdering Plagueis.<ref name="DP" /> Sidious, under the guise of [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] Palpatine, was elected [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]<ref name="Episode I">{{Film|I}}</ref> and masterminded a devastating [[Clone Wars/Legends|galactic war]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy]].<ref name="Episode II">{{Film|II}}</ref> His double identity allowed him to infiltrate, deceive and eventually destroy the Republic and nearly the Jedi. After becoming the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] of the newly formed [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], he brought the Galaxy under the control of the Sith, bringing about their foretold [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|revenge]].<ref name="Episode III">{{Film|III}}</ref>

[[File:Sidious_Maul.png|thumb|right|275px|Darth Sidious with his first apprentice, Darth Maul]]
Sidious broke the Rule of Two at least twice: once by training [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] while still under the tutelage of Darth Plagueis;<ref name="DP" /> and secondly, by taking on two apprentices at once, and in the form of two Jedi: [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], the former [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] of the legendary [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], dubbed Darth Tyranus,<ref name="Episode II" /> and the [[Fosh/Legends|Fosh]] Jedi [[Vergere]]. Vergere was said to be merely a candidate and not a "true" apprentice, and apparently left after discovering the depths of Sidious's madness.<ref name="LotF:B" /> In Maul's case, Plagueis had been informed of his existence and purpose by Sidious before Sidious began training him. With regard to Maul, Plagueis and Sidious had planned from the start for him to be nothing more than a disposable weapon and not a true Sith Lord. As such, neither Sidious nor Plagueis considered his existence to be a violation of the Rule, not even when Sidious bestowed the title of "Darth" upon him. It also appears that Sidious considered offering Tyranus a place at his side prior to Maul's defeat, although details on the timing are vague and, as previously stated, Sidious did not consider Maul to be a true apprentice.<ref name="DP" /> In any case, Sidious secretly intended to create a [[Rule of One (Palpatine's Doctrine)|new doctrine]] that ensured he was the permanent ruling Sith Lord, and that his apprentices would merely be useful tools rather than usurpers.<ref name="BoS: SftDS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>

[[File:Sidious_Tyranus.png|thumb|left|275px|Darth Sidious with his second apprentice, Darth Tyranus]]
Darth Tyranus pledged to personally teach young [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]] in the ways of the dark side, and privately referred to her as "apprentice," and she addressed him as "Master."<ref name="TCW|Nightsisters">{{TCW|Nightsisters (episode)}}</ref><ref name="TCW|Witches of the Mist">{{TCW|Witches of the Mist}}</ref> Tyranus never bestowed the title of Darth to Ventress, perhaps out of respect for the Rule of Two. She certainly believed their master/apprentice status to be genuine,<ref name="TCW|Nightsisters" /><ref name="TCW|Witches of the Mist" /><ref name="TCW|To Catch a Jedi">{{TCW|To Catch a Jedi}}</ref> and in any case it can be heralded as a sign of Tyranus' rising ambitions. Sidious sensed a disturbance in the Force concerning Ventress. He considered her enough of a potential threat that he ordered Tyranus to eliminate her as a test of his continued loyalty. Tyranus acquiesced and, while disavowing Ventress as his apprentice, turned his fleet's own guns on her at the [[Battle of Sullust/Legends|Battle of Sullust]].<ref name="TCW|Nightsisters" /> Erroneously giving Ventress up for dead, Tyranus soon after took [[Savage Opress/Legends|Savage Opress]] as a new Sith apprentice with the ultimate goal of overthrowing Sidious and ruling the galaxy together,<ref name="TCW|Monster">{{TCW|Monster}}</ref> though that plan did not come to fruition either, as he was a puppet for Ventress who survived her master's betrayal and attempted to use Savage as pawn to kill her master which failed.<ref name="TCW|Witches of the Mist" />

Maul, after narrowly surviving his duel with Obi-Wan Kenobi and faking his death, broke the Rule of Two as well. Shortly after returning from his exile and uniting with his brother, Maul declared himself Opress's master and demonstrated his superiority over Opress.<ref name="TCW|Revival">{{TCW|Revival (episode)}}</ref> He remarked that there could only be two&mdash;yet in his decision he had created two rival pairs of Sith. However Darth Sidious eventually corrected this oversight by searching them out and single-handedly [[Battle of Mandalore/Legends|defeating both in mortal combat]] and killing Opress, preserving the Rule of Two. Only Maul survived the battle, but Sidious decided that his former apprentice could be of further use to him.<ref name="TCW|The Lawless" />

After eventually deciding that it was time for him to make [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] his apprentice, Sidious [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|staged Palpatine's kidnapping]], in order for Anakin to kill Tyranus and then replace him. While Tyranus knew about the plan to capture the Chancellor, he was unaware that he would be sacrificed. Anakin defeated Tyranus in the battle. Sidious then betrayed Tyranus by having him killed by Skywalker. Not too long after, Skywalker betrayed he Jedi, fell to the dark side and became Sidious apprentice, with Sidious naming him Darth Vader. After gaining Vader, Sidious unleashed his<ref name="Episode III" /> [[Order 66/Legends|secret protocol]] to [[Inhibitor chip/Legends|forcibly compel]]<ref name="TCW|Orders">{{TCW|Orders (episode)}}</ref> the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Republic's army]] to turn against the Jedi, leading to the defeat and near destruction of the Jedi Order and rise of the Galactic Empire.<ref name="Episode III" />

===Imperial Period===
Sidious and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] trained and employed a number of [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] and other [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] agents such as the Dark Acolytes, the [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitorius]], and the [[Dark Side Elite]]. As these agents were not taught the secrets of the Sith and were considered merely [[Sith acolyte/Legends|acolytes]], not apprentices, they did not consider this a violation of the Rule of Two. However, the fact that Tyranus sought to replace the Jedi Order with a Sith army, the so-called [[Fist of the Empire (group)|Fist of the Empire]], indicated that he had envisioned the abolition of the Rule of Two once the Sith took over the galaxy.<ref name="ROTSN">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref>

Just as Sidious had taken Darth Maul as an apprentice before truly ascending to the rank of Master, Vader took it upon himself to train a secret apprentice of his own. Vader's physical and psychological traumas had diminished his potential in the Force, and he did not believe himself capable of overthrowing Sidious, the most powerful Sith Lord in history, alone. To that end, he endeavored to mentor an exceptionally powerful Force-wielder who would not only serve as his personal assassin, but would one day stand with him to overthrow Sidious. Thus for several years, [[Galen Marek]], codenamed ''Starkiller'', was trained in the ways of the Sith and the dark side of the Force. Marek became a merciless assassin, devoted to the goal of destroying Sidious in order to become a true Sith Lord. Vader later changed his mind about using Marek to overthrow Sidious and attempted to kill him. Marek survived, and went on not only to redeem himself, but to provide the impetus for the formation of the Rebel Alliance.<ref name="TFUvg">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref>

Marek would defeat Vader. Seeing this as an opportunity to replace and be rid of Vader, Sidious ordered Marek to finish Vader, but Marek instead, refused, and subsequently redeemed himself and attacked Sidious. Marek ended up using all his energy to kill the stormtroopers and destroy much of the dome, but ended up dying in the process.<ref name="TFUvg" />

[[File:Vader_Sidious.png|thumb|right|275px|Darth Sidious and his third apprentice, Darth Vader]]
Despite Marek's unanticipated redemption and subsequent death, Vader refused to lose an extremely powerful asset and resorted to relying on the [[Cloning/Legends|cloning technology]] of [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]], and thus continued to violate the Rule of Two by creating a clone of Marek to replace his former apprentice. After many failed experiments, including a [[Subject 1138|rogue clone]] who escaped from the [[Timira City]] Cloning Facility, Vader succeeded in achieving his goal by creating a [[Dark Apprentice|perfect clone]] who wielded all of Marek's strengths, but none of his weaknesses.<ref name="TFU2vg">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]''</ref>

Despite all of the strengths of the Rule of Two, Bane overlooked two critical weaknesses in his philosophy: the first, and the one of most concern to Bane, was the possibility the Master might spend most of their lifetime training an unworthy apprentice. Later in his life, Bane believed this to be the case with his apprentice Zannah. Aging poorly due to a lifetime of immersion in the dark side, and with Zannah apparently content to toil in his shadow, Bane desperately sought out the secrets to eternal life in order to buy himself enough time to train a truly worthy apprentice. His fears for Zannah came to naught, as she had in fact been preparing to kill him even as he had begun to worry that she was simply waiting for him to age to the point where he would be an easy kill. Zannah proved herself worthy by dueling and very narrowly [[Duel on Ambria (980 BBY)|defeating]] Bane on [[Ambria/Legends|Ambria]], and continued the Rule with an apprentice of her own.<ref name="DB:DoE">''[[Darth Bane: Dynasty of Evil]]''</ref> The possibility of training a failed apprentice would go on to irk other Sith Masters like [[Darth Cognus]], whose [[Darth Millennial|first apprentice]] left her over ideological differences.<ref name="Evil Never Dies" /> Additionally, despite being the very inspiration for the Rule of Two,<ref name="DB: PoD" /> Revan renouncing the dark side and killing [[Darth Malak|the reigning Sith Lord]] served as proof of Darth Bane overlooking another critical weakness in his Rule&mdash;that one of the Sith Lords could be redeemed while killing the other at the same time.<ref name="SW:KotOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref>

In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], during the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], Sidious had the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], his apprentice's son, fight against Darth Vader so he could become his new apprentice. After Skywalker defeated Vader, Sidious betrayed his apprentice by ordering Skywalker to kill him, but Skywalker refused to slay his father, so Sidious decided to unleash his wrath on him through [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]]. Unable to let his son die at the hands of his master, Anakin Skywalker killed Darth Sidious in a selfless act of sacrifice and succeeded to redeem himself of the life he lived as Darth Vader. Without Sidious or Vader, the Order of the Sith Lords was effectively dissolved since its only two members were dead. As a result, it appeared that there were no others to carry on the Order's traditions and teachings, and the Rule of Two was veritably destroyed.<ref name="Episode VI">{{Film|VI}}</ref>

[[File:Vader_Starkiller.png|thumb|left|275px|Darth Vader acknowledging Starkiller as his apprentice, thus breaking the Rule of Two]]
Lumiya, one of Vader's secret apprentices and a former [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hand]], declared herself ''Dark Lady of the Sith'' and established her own [[Lumiya's Sith|Sith Order]].<ref name="Evil Never Dies" /> She remained faithful to Darth Bane's ancient diktat, the Rule of Two,<ref name="LotF:B" /> by taking [[Flint]] as her first apprentice and then [[Carnor Jax]] as her second.<ref name="Evil Never Dies" /> Her third and final apprentice was Darth Caedus, the grandson of Darth Vader and formerly known as Jacen Solo.<ref name="LotF:B" /> Lumiya was ultimately [[Duel on Terephon|killed]] by Luke Skywalker after Solo murdered Skywalker's wife [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]].<ref name="LotF:S">''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]''</ref> Prior to her death, however, Lumiya instructed Caedus to find an apprentice for himself. He fulfilled her last wish after finding a suitable apprentice in [[Tahiri Veila]], a fallen [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] whose emotional attachment to Caedus's [[Anakin Solo|dead brother]] brought about her fall to the dark side.<ref name="LotF:R">''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]''</ref> However, Caedus's death, alongside Veila's turning back to the light side shortly beforehand, brought an end to the Rule of Two for good.<ref name="LotF:I">''[[Legacy of the Force: Invincible]]''</ref>

===Abandonment===
By the year [[130 ABY]], a [[One Sith|new Sith Order]] emerged under the leadership of [[Darth Krayt]], thus taking the place of the former Order of the Sith Lords. Unlike Bane's Order, Krayt abolished the Rule of Two and replaced it with the [[Rule of One]], with one Dark Lord of the Sith representing the Order itself, while also commanding many Lords, acolytes, and minions.<ref name="L5: B,P4">[[Legacy (2006) 5|''Legacy'' (2006) 5]]</ref>

His revision of the Sith was met with extreme disapproval and outrage, particularly from the gatekeeper of [[Darth Bane's holocron]]. When Krayt sought the wisdom of the ancient Sith Lords, they rebuffed him as an offensive heretic and a ''false'' Sith. [[Darth Nihilus' holocron|Darth Nihilus]] did not provide Krayt with helpful information, [[Holocron of Heresies|Darth Andeddu]] accused him of heresy, and Darth Bane warned the Rule of One would be the death of Krayt and the entire Sith.<ref name="L5: B,P4" /> In the end, however, Krayt was [[Battle of Coruscant (Second Imperial Civil War)|finally killed]] by [[Cade Skywalker]] and the One Sith retreated to reexamine how to retake the galaxy.<ref name="L—W6">[[Legacy — War 6|''Legacy — War'' 6]]</ref>

===Surviving Adherents===
By [[138 ABY]], at least one Sith known as [[Darth Wredd]] still believed in the philosophy of the Rule of Two, and ended up [[Darth Wredd's insurgency|wiping out]] the One Sith to re-establish it.<ref name="L18">[[Legacy (2013) 18|''Legacy'' (2013) 18]]</ref> However, this ironically led to the assumed extinction of the Sith as a whole, as his attempt at [[Yalta Val|procuring]] an apprentice failed, with him dying at the hands of [[Ania Solo]].<ref name="Legacy Volume 2">[[Star Wars: Legacy Volume 2|''Star Wars: Legacy'' Volume 2]]</ref> Some, such as the [[Marasiah Fel|Empress Fel]] doubted the Sith were gone and indeed a few such as [[Darth Talon]] were not known to be among the slain.<ref name="L18" /><ref name="L—W6" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Don't get any clever ideas, kid.|Palpatine to Vader, referring to the Rule of Two|<ref name="LEGO Star Wars: The Dark Side">''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Dark Side]]''</ref>}}

The Rule of Two was first mentioned in ''[[Episode I: The Phantom Menace]]'' and its [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|novelization]] by [[Terry Brooks]]. The rule was not named as the "Rule of Two" in either; it became known as such by fans by May 2000.<ref name="first ref this page ever had">{{WebCite|url=https://wso.williams.edu/~rfoxwell/starwars/TPM/RuleOfTwo.htm|text=The Rule of Two|author=Chris Foxwell|archivedate=20000522134141|nolive=1}}</ref>

[[Timeline of galactic history/Legends|Chronologically]], [[Darth Rivan]] predates Darth Bane,<ref name="JvsS: TEGttF" /> yet one of the traps in Darth Rivan's fortress, as shown in ''[[A Mon Alone]]'', is based on the Sith adherence to the Rule of Two.<ref name="AMA">{{LivingForce|A Mon Alone}}</ref> However, Rivan did not pre-date Darth Revan, and in fact based his name off of the historical texts of Revan,<ref name="JvsS: TEGttF" /> whose teachings about apprentices inspired Darth Bane to implement the Rule of Two.<ref name="DB: PoD" />

On [[Hypori/Legends|Hypori]] around [[54 BBY/Legends|54 BBY]], Darth Plagueis said to his apprentice Darth Sidious that rather than the tens of thousands of Jedi, only thirty in a millennium were fit to be Sith, implying that the Rule of Two spanned at least 30 individuals, including or up until him and his apprentice.<ref name="DP" />
